protester.name: Apex Federal
strengths: Factor 1: Proposed 99.999% SLA exceeds requirements with multi-region FedRAMP High government cloud architecture.
Factor 2: Dr. Elena Vance possesses 14 years of federal cloud experience, active Certified Cloud Solutions Architect Professional, Certified Federal Cloud Fellow, and CISSP certifications.
Factor 2: All three key personnel exceed mandatory experience thresholds with verified records.
weaknesses: Factor 1: Significant Weakness 1 (UNSTATED CRITERIA): The TET assigned a Significant Weakness because Apex "did not propose a dedicated on-premises physical datacenter hardware bridge facility to connect with legacy Baltimore CMS mainframe hardware." (Note: Section L & M do not mention or require on-premises physical datacenter hardware).

personnel.certifications: Certified Cloud Solutions Architect - Professional (Active #CSA-99281), Certified Federal Cloud Fellow, CISSP (#498210, Current).

references.title: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services - Current Cloud Platform (Incumbent Contract)
Defense Health Agency (DHA) - Electronic Health Record Cloud Enclave

awardee.name: Nexus Systems
strengths: Factor 1: Commercial microservice architecture is modular and cost-efficient.
weaknesses: Factor 1: Note on SLA (FAILURE TO ENFORCE MANDATORY MINIMUM): The TET noted that Nexus proposed a 99.95% availability SLA. The TET determined that "99.95% is acceptable for general web workloads," despite Section L.3.1 mandating a 99.99% minimum threshold. No deficiency was assigned.

Factor 2: Note on Lead Architect (DISPARATE TREATMENT / WAIVER OF MANDATORY MINIMUM): The TET evaluated Johnathan Brooks (Lead Cloud Architect). Although Mr. Brooks possesses only 4 years of cloud experience and lacks Cloud Architect Professional and CISSP certifications (Section L.4 mandated 10 years, Cloud Architect Professional, and CISSP), the TET stated: "The candidate possesses good commercial aptitude which compensates for the shortage in required years of experience." A rating of Acceptable was awarded.

Factor 3: Note on Relevance (FLAWED EVALUATION): Evaluated Retail Storefront Portal ($3.2M) and State DMV ($8.5M). Even though neither contract met the Section L.5 relevance threshold ($50M+ total value, FedRAMP High, federal healthcare cloud), the TET concluded that "commercial web hosting demonstrates general competence."
